units.translation: It seems that Thebes in Egypt was founded first, as Xenagoras says in Book 1 of his Chronicles (240 FGrH 1 J.). And Nicanor also says in his Renamings (FGrH 15 M. III 634) that the city of Thebes was founded first in Egypt, himself agreeing with Archemachus (FGrH 6 M. IV 315).

Hippys (FGrH 1 M. II 13) conjectures that the Egyptians were the first to come into being from the temperament of the air and from the fact that the water of the Nile is most productive. Apollonius says that they existed before all the stars appeared; for which reason they are thought to have observed their nature and given them names, and they called the twelve zodiac signs "counselor gods," and the planets "rod-bearers."

Herodotus (loc. cit.) says that the Phrygians were the first to come into being. Later Psammetichus, king of the Egyptians, wishing to determine who were the earth-born, handed over two infants to a shepherd, ordering that no one speak, but only that a goat's teat be given to them.
